stimuli.text:
Scenario

Imagine you are traveling very far away, and meet a new group of people you know nothing about. You are trying to learn about the people, the society, and the language all at the same time.

There is a person in this group called Paji. Paji has more power and influence than the other people in the group. Leaders in this society vary in how much they care about justice and treating people fairly, and whether they have biases towards some people.

You hear that Paji has a strong sense of justice and tries to make sure everyone is treated fairly.

There's an action in this society which is called daxing. You don't know anything about daxing.

People in this society have something they call 'jats', which really matter to them.

During the week, Paji goes around and checks how everyone else is acting. After all, some people may be harming others or acting selfishly, and in response, Paji could either do nothing, take away half of their jats, or take away all of their jats.

What do you know so far?

queries.prompt: In this society, how morally wrong is daxing?
In general, how much does Paji care about justice and acting fairly?
How harmful is daxing?
Who has power and influence in this society?
